question: How the technology screen's detail panel fills its `effects` list box with `detail_entry` rows: where the text comes from, how it is cut into rows, for which level, and when it is refilled.

addresses.name: CTechnologyView::ShowDetails
addresses.comment:
**The panel for one technology.** Sets +0xD0 (details_shown) and keeps the technology at +0xD4; hides `tech_categories` and shows `tech_details`. `photo` is the file <base>/pictures/tech/<key>.tga made a sprite from the GFX_no_tech_image definition when the file exists; `name` is the name + ' (' + level + 1 + ')', always ' (1)' for a technology with no additional_offset; `name_expl` is GetTechnologyLevelName; `icon_finish_type` gets the sprite 'icon_' + the on_completion category's key with **no '_small'** - the full picture, where a tree entry takes the small one; `input_box`, `difficulty` and `year` as on a tree entry; `tech_status_finnished` for a finished one-level technology; `desc` is GetTechnologyDescription.

**The level** (one local, 0x81D945 and 0x81E71F): `levels = the played country's level_by_technology[Index] + 1`, set to **1 where additional_offset (+0x2C0) is 0**; no cap at max_level. The same local feeds `year`, `desc` and the effects - the rule the tree entry's tooltip uses.

**`effects`** (0x81E812..0x81EF8A, read whole): text = CTechStatistics::BuildEffectsText(technology, levels, no unit filter, the played country) - the tree entry tooltip's effects block. The list (`effects`) gets slots 21 then 23 (hide, empty - the reading earlier views' records give these slots). One `detail_entry` row (a 0x28-byte list item from the gui factory 0xA8BBD0) is made at once, its `text` set to '' and added (list slot 4); its `text` box (an instantTextBoxType) supplies the font (+0x54, looked up in the graphics' font tables +0x88 then +0x94) and the width (max_width +0x8C, its low word). A CTextLayout is built on the stack with that font, its area written directly as width = max_width (330 in the shipped file) and height = 2000, SetText(text), and the text replaced by GetLaidOutText - the wrap's breaks made newlines. That is split at '\n' (0xA5B520, every piece kept, empty ones and an empty tail included). Then for each piece in order: **a piece shorter than 2 bytes is skipped**; otherwise the current row's `text` is set to it unchanged (no colour carried, nothing trimmed) and the row resized (window slot 25) to **180** wide by the height the text box answers (its slot 47, second short); and **only where another piece follows** a new empty row is made and added. So every line of 2 bytes or more is a row, and a text ending in a newline - every non-empty BuildEffectsText ends so - leaves one empty row at the bottom at the row window's declared size. Last, list slot 20 (show). No scroll position is kept. `ret 8`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
addresses.evidence: Signature: both arguments are read off the frame - [ebp+0xC] is stored to +0xD4 at 0x81D4FE and [ebp+8] is the view throughout - and the function ends `ret 8`; all four callers push the technology then the view (0x678213, 0x817911, 0x818166, 0x81CD46). The effects list: read instruction by instruction from 0x81E812 to the vector's destructor at 0x81EF8A - BuildEffectsText at 0x81E846 with [esp+0x38] (the level local, written only at 0x81D94C and 0x81E71F at base depth; every other `[esp+0x38]` store sits under two pushes); 'effects' pushed at 0x81E85A; the first 'detail_entry' row at 0x81E8ED..0x81EAF5 with text '' (0x15B4945, an empty literal); font lookup 0xA77F90 at 0x81EB14/0x81EB27; CTextLayout::CTextLayout 0x81EB52; width word from [textbox+0x8C] and 0x7D0 written to layout +0x48/+0x4A at 0x81EB89/0x81EBA9; SetText 0x81EBB1, GetLaidOutText 0x81EBC5; split 0xA5B520 with 0xA at 0x81EC14; the `cmp [esp+0x110], 2; jge` size test at 0x81ECA4; the 0xB4 width at 0x81EDA6; the iterator test before the new row at 0x81EDDF..0x81EDF7. The splitter keeps empty pieces: 0xA5B520 pushes substr(start, pos) for every hit and substr(start, size) for the tail with no length test. What would show it wrong: a second writer of the level local at base depth, or a test on the line's content other than its length - neither is in the listing. The entry stays inferred for the parts carried over from fragments/merged/country-views.json, which were not re-read here.
addresses.revises: Signature added (it had only no_signature, which said the technology was not traced: it is the second stack argument). The effects clause said 'BuildEffectsText split into lines, each a detail_entry window with its text set'; it now gives the level (country's + 1, 1 for a one-level technology), the wrap at the text box's max_width with a CTextLayout, the split, the skipping of pieces under 2 bytes, the 180-wide rows, the trailing empty row and the absence of any colour carry-over.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::RefreshTechnologyDetails
addresses.comment: Slot 102, beside RefreshDiplomacyView (slot 101). Where the open view (+0xCFC) is 2, the views vector (+0xD00) holds more than two, view 2's slot 7 (IsOpen) answers true and its selected_technology (+0xD4) is set: CTechnologyView::ShowDetails(view 2, that technology). **details_shown (+0xD0) is not tested**, so the panel is made again whether or not it was up. Bare `ret`. Called only through the in-game screen (CCurrentGameState +0xBE8) from slot 6 of the six custom-game research commands - CCgmSetStageCommand, CCgmTechResearchChangeCommand, CCgmTechResearchResetCommand, CCgmTechResearchClearAllCommand, CCgmTechResearchExecuteStackedCommand and CCgmTechResearchSetProgressCommand. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
addresses.evidence: 0x6781D0..0x67821B read whole: `cmp [esi+0xcfc], 2`, `(end - begin) & ~3 > 8`, `[eax+8]` slot 7 (`[edx+0x1c]`), `[eax+0xd4]` non-null, push tech, push view, call 0x81D400, `ret`. The only holder is CInGameIdler's table 0x15CEB54 at slot 102 (.rdata 0x15CECEC; no other vftable holds it, no direct call in .text). Callers: a scan of .text for `mov reg,[reg+0x198]` followed by `call reg`, and `call [reg+0x198]`, finds the six Execute bodies (0x428E33, 0x42AC74, 0x42B2E2, 0x42B9A3, 0x42BD2F, 0x42C0CA), each on `[[0x1A89790]+0xBE8]`; their classes from the RTTI export (slot 6 of each table). What would show it wrong: another call through a different encoding (a computed slot), which the scan would not see.

addresses.name: CTechTreeEntry::OpenDetails
addresses.comment: The handler CTechTreeEntry::CTechTreeEntry installs in its observer glue at +4 (the first of its two, beside 0x818170): CTechnologyView::ShowDetails(view +0x3C, technology +0x30). So pressing a tree entry makes the detail panel for its technology. Which of the entry's button events reaches it was not traced. Bare `ret`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
addresses.evidence: 0x818160..0x81816D: `mov eax,[ecx+0x30]; mov ecx,[ecx+0x3c]; push eax; push ecx; call 0x81D400; ret`. Its address is written into the glue at 0x817958 inside the constructor 0x817920 (`mov [esi+8], 0x818160`). +0x30 and +0x3C are the entry's recorded technology and view, which is what ties ECX to the entry rather than to the glue. What would show it wrong: a dispatcher that hands the handler the glue's own address - then +0x30/+0x3C would not be the technology and the view, and ShowDetails's own reads would fault.

addresses.name: CCurrentResearchEntry::OpenDetails
addresses.comment: The handler CCurrentResearchEntry::CCurrentResearchEntry installs (0x8153FA): where the line's technology (+0xC8) has a Folder (+0x290), that folder becomes the view's selected_folder (+0x15C) and CTechnologyView::BuildTree(view) lays the tree out for it; then CTechnologyView::ShowDetails(view +0x210, technology). So pressing a line of the queue switches the tree to the technology's folder and makes its panel. Bare `ret`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
addresses.evidence: 0x8178E0..0x817919 read whole: `mov eax,[esi+0xc8]; mov eax,[eax+0x290]`; when non-zero `mov [ecx+0x15c], eax` with ecx = [esi+0x210], `push ecx; call 0x821570`; then push [esi+0xC8], push [esi+0x210], call 0x81D400; `ret`. The constructor 0x815330 writes the address at 0x8153FA and stores its 2nd, 3rd and 4th stack arguments at +0xCC, +0xC8 and +0x210 (0x815453, 0x815448, 0x81550D). What would show it wrong: as for the tree entry, a dispatcher passing the glue (at +0x28) instead of the entry.

addresses.name: CTechnologyView::KeepDetails
addresses.comment: Slot 3: `mov byte [ecx+0xB8], 1; ret` - keep_details. CTechnologyView::Show re-makes the detail panel for the kept technology only where this byte is set, and clears it; otherwise it clears details_shown and shows the skills. The base CCountryView leaves slot 3 to the shared empty stub 0xABF890; CProductionView's slot 3 (0x7FFA70) sets its own +0xCC the same way. Who calls slot 3 was not traced. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
addresses.evidence: The body is two instructions, held only by CTechnologyView's table 0x15DFC44 at slot 3. Its reader: Show at 0x81CC4B (`cmp byte [ebx+0xb8],0; jne`; else `mov byte [ebx+0xd0],0`), 0x81CC62 clears it, 0x81CC69 tests +0xD0 and 0x81CD3C..0x81CD48 calls ShowDetails when +0xD4 is set. The name rests on that one reader (inferred); the body is confirmed.

struct_fields.name: keep_details
struct_fields.comment: Set by slot 3 (KeepDetails). CTechnologyView::Show keeps the detail panel and makes it again for selected_technology only where it is set, and clears it; where it is clear, details_shown (+0xD0) is cleared and the skills are shown. CDiplomacyView uses the same offset as a rebuild flag of its own, so it may be one CCountryView byte; not checked. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
struct_fields.evidence: Written 1 at 0x81D130 (slot 3); read at 0x81CC4B and cleared at 0x81CC62 in Show (0x81C9B0).

struct_fields.name: view
struct_fields.comment: The technology screen: the constructor's fourth stack argument, handed to CTechnologyView::ShowDetails as its view and given the technology's folder at +0x15C by OpenDetails. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 5.5.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored at 0x81550D from [ebp+0x14]; read at 0x8178EF and passed as ShowDetails's first argument at 0x817912, and as BuildTree's at 0x8178F9.
